clue.text: Unglazed earthenware (seconds) for English cookies

parts.note: biscuit is pottery fired once but not yet glazed

explanation.surface: A potter swaps cheap seconds of plain clay ware for some English cookies.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, sweet baked treats Americans call cookies are called biscuits, and biscuit is also the potter's word for fired, unglazed ware.
explanation.definitionFit: What Americans call cookies the British call by this name.

clue.text: Costume appropriate for a Pacific atoll

definitions.meaning: a bathing costume, the two-piece kind
the Marshall Islands atoll used for US nuclear tests

explanation.definitionFit: The two-piece swimsuit was named after the Marshall Islands atoll where atom bombs were tested in 1946.

clue.text: Wheelless vehicle left in marshland grass

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: sedge is a grasslike plant of wet ground

explanation.surface: A cart without wheels is abandoned among the reeds of a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled runs on runners over snow rather than on wheels.

clue.text: Overthrows the aristocratic classes?

definitions.meaning: knocks over or topples
read as ..., the upper sets or strata of society

explanation.definitionFit: Toppling things means knocking them over; split as up sets it means society's upper groups.

clue.text: To flee, catch a scheduled plane

definitions.meaning: to run away
literally board a timetabled air service

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for running away, read literally as boarding a timetabled air service.

clue.text: Cartridge sought by kerb crawler

definitions.meaning: the stylus unit on a record player's tone arm
a kerb crawler drives slowly looking for a prostitute to collect

explanation.definitionFit: The cartridge holding a turntable's needle has this name, and a casual sexual partner found in the street is also one.

clue.text: Metal straightedge which is totally inflexible

definitions.meaning: a ruler made of a hard metal
a law or regime admitting no exceptions

explanation.definitionFit: A harsh regime allowing no exceptions, read literally as a ruler made of hard metal.

clue.text: What a roadman has to do is stop approaching people

definitions.text: What a roadman has to do
definitions.meaning: a roadman maintains a road, read as minding a route
an order not to come near

explanation.definitionFit: The warning not to come near, split as maintaining a route, a roadman's job.

clue.text: Get jobs for the big boys who enjoy jobs for the boys

definitions.text: Get jobs for the big boys
definitions.meaning: read as ..., find posts for adult males

definitions.text: who enjoy jobs for the boys
definitions.meaning: people given office through patronage

explanation.definitionFit: People appointed through political patronage, read as an instruction to find posts for adult males.

clue.text: It reminds one to stock eastern wine

parts.note: to stock goods is to keep them

explanation.surface: A note urging someone to lay in some Oriental wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a memento whose purpose is to bring back memories.

clue.text: Not applicable to the way one discovers an Italian city

indicators.note: joined to means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a certain route has nothing to do with how one finds a city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Modena is a city in Emilia-Romagna, northern Italy, home of balsamic vinegar.

clue.text: Free evening spent close to very loud music

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone spends their evening off beside deafening music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' is only a link here; 'very loud music' points to the score marking FF.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker's evening away from duty is time free of their job.

clue.text: An acre ploughed up in secret

indicators.note: turning over a field with a plough churns it, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A field of one acre is ploughed in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane knowledge is mysterious and known only to a few initiates.

clue.text: Concealed anger about a writing desk

indicators.note: the outer letters go round the single letter

explanation.surface: Someone hides their fury over a bureau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the A between the T and the I, so the single letter lands in the middle of the two joined words rather than inside the anger alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretaire is a bureau or escritoire with a fold-down writing surface.

clue.text: Unwatched barman's last request to customers

definitions.meaning: a person without a watch must ask a stranger for the hour
the call a British publican makes at closing time

explanation.definitionFit: The polite question a watchless person asks a passer-by is also the landlord's closing call in a British pub.

clue.text: Account presented to a parson is absolutely right

indicators.note: one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: A bill handed to a clergyman turns out to be quite correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precise and free from error is exactly correct.

clue.text: Record success with an overhead volley

definitions.meaning: a best-selling song or disc
a tennis smash, struck down hard from above the head

explanation.definitionFit: A chart-topping record, read literally as a tennis smash struck from above the head.

clue.text: Make a supreme effort to visit London

definitions.meaning: to do something lavishly and with great energy
literally travel into the capital, called town in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, going up to town means going to London.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for going all out, read literally as travelling into the capital.

clue.text: Mob of cattle kept on public land?

definitions.meaning: the masses, ordinary rabble
a herd of cows grazing on the village common

explanation.definitionFit: A disparaging term for the rabble or masses, read literally as a herd of beasts grazing a common.

clue.text: I learn differentiation in one dimension

indicators.note: a mathematical term here doubling as a signal to make the letters different in order

explanation.surface: A student says they are studying calculus along a single axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear measures run along a single straight line, involving only one dimension.

clue.text: Scripture class teaches how to abandon one's wicked ways

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject once called scripture
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A religious studies lesson teaches pupils to give up sin.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class, and RE (religious education) is where scripture is taught.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend one's ways is to change for the better and give up bad behaviour.

clue.text: Boy swallowing cannabis is 15

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

explanation.surface: A lad has eaten some marijuana.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference to 15-down, meaning absolutely right; 'swallowing' takes the drug into the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly correct, matching the sense of 15-down, absolutely right.

clue.text: Result of anti-aircraft fire

definitions.meaning: the outcome or consequence
shells fired upward at planes, read as shot aimed skyward

explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome of events, read literally as gunfire sent skyward.

clue.text: Start playing when industrial action is rampant

parts.note: a strike is a stoppage of work
a rampant heraldic beast stands up on its hind legs, so up stands for it

explanation.surface: A band begins to play while a wave of walkouts sweeps the country.
explanation.definitionFit: When a band begins a tune they are said to launch into it with this phrase.

clue.text: Israeli port has odd layout

indicators.note: a layout is an arrangement, so these letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: An Israeli harbour town has an unusual street plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashdod is Israel's largest port, on the Mediterranean south of Tel Aviv.

clue.text: Annihilated by a blackboard duster

definitions.meaning: destroyed completely
what happens to chalk writing when the board is cleaned

explanation.definitionFit: Destroyed utterly, and literally what a duster does to chalk on the board.

clue.text: Net tax adjustment not yet expired

indicators.note: an adjustment alters something, here the order of these letters

explanation.surface: A revision to net tax is still in force.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still in existence, not lost or died out, is described this way.

clue.text: Inebriated chaps those Sherwood Foresters

parts.note: merry is a mild word for tipsy

explanation.surface: Some drunken fellows turn out to be Robin Hood's outlaw band.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherwood Forest is the legendary home of Robin Hood and his outlaw band.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood's outlaw companions in Sherwood Forest are known by this name.
